allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

ambiguities.description: Open ambiguities this step could not settle; each names what it is about. An item is deleted once its answer is applied.

rules.description: Array of governance rules. A rule is one requirement on how the project is changed or released, with the upstream reason it exists and, optionally, who enforces it: a command named in cli_command, or a person (enforcer 'review'). A rule with neither is meant to be enforced by a CI job of step 12 that names it in its `realises`. At least one rule.

items.description: A single governance rule: id, text, upstream reason, optional enforcer.

rule_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this governance rule. Format: rule-{what-is-required}. Example: 'rule-contract-tests-on-every-pr'. Should be stable across spec versions. Anti-pattern: rule-1 (non-descriptive).

text.description: The governance requirement, as one falsifiable sentence a person or a command can check. Example: 'Every pull request runs the contract test suite before merge.' Anti-pattern: 'Follow good review practice' (not checkable).

enforcer.description: Who enforces this rule when it is not a command or a job. The only value is 'review': a person decides. Omit it for a rule a CI job enforces (that job names the rule in its own `realises`) and for a rule that names a command in cli_command. A rule never carries both enforcer and cli_command.

cli_command.description: Name of the specdev command that checks this rule, as listed in the CLI command list that registry-generate writes. Example: 'spec-check'. Omit for a review rule and for a rule a CI job enforces. A rule never carries both enforcer and cli_command.

derives_from.description: Ids of the upstream nodes that give this rule its reason: a charter constraint, risk or scope item, an environment or gate of step 02a, or an approver-only stakeholder. At least one. Example: ["risk-reset-link-takeover"]. Anti-pattern: leaving a rule without a reason, or naming a functional requirement here.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this rule relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this rule: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

scope.description: Delivery scope for this rule: 'in' for the current release (the default when the field is omitted), 'later' for deferred work, 'out' for explicitly excluded work. 'later' and 'out' require scope_reason.

scope_reason.description: Why this rule is 'later' or 'out' of scope. Required when scope is 'later' or 'out'.

aliases.description: Former ids of this rule; `specdev node rename` adds the old id here. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this rule replaces. Optional.

versioning.description: Versioning scheme applied to spec artifacts. Decision rule: use 'semver' for public APIs or schemas with explicit breaking-change semantics (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH); use 'date-based' for internal artifact versioning where freshness matters more than compatibility (YYYY-MM-DD); use 'sequential' for simple monotonic increment when breaking changes are managed out-of-band. Examples: public REST API → 'semver'; internal spec artifacts → 'date-based'. Anti-pattern: using 'sequential' for public APIs (consumers cannot determine breaking changes from the version number alone).

commit_message_rules.description: Rules for the format of commit messages. `specdev governance-check --message` reads them and checks the one message it is given; it checks commit messages only.

require_spec_ids.description: When true and `pattern` is set, governance-check fails a message that does not match `pattern`. When false, or when `pattern` is absent, it accepts any message. It does not check that an id named in the message exists. Spec ids that may appear in a message, written in brackets (e.g., [fr-user-login]), begin with one of these prefixes: fr-* (functional requirements), api-* (API contracts), cap-* (capabilities), nfr-* (non-functional requirements), inv-* (invariants), fix-* (fixtures), ms-* (milestones), ext-* (extensions). Anti-pattern: a prefix not in this list (e.g., req-*, feat-*) — use the canonical prefixes so a reader can find the node.

pattern.description: Regular expression that governance-check matches against the start of a commit message when require_spec_ids is true. A pattern that expects a bracketed artifact id keeps commits tied to spec changes, as in 'feat(spec): add login flow [fr-user-login]'. Conventional Commits format is recommended: '<type>(<scope>): <summary> [<artifact-id>]'.

id_pattern_ref.description: Canonical reference to the ID pattern used in commit messages. Kind is structurally pinned to 'id_pattern'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:id_pattern:conventional-commit", "kind": "id_pattern"}. Omit if the pattern is fully defined by the 'pattern' field.

error_message.description: Human-readable rejection message shown when a commit fails pattern validation. Should list the allowed commit types and provide a valid example. Example: 'Commit must match: feat|fix|chore|docs(spec): description [artifact-id]. Example: feat(spec): add login flow [fr-user-login]'.

policy_ref.description: Canonical reference to the governance policy. Kind is structurally pinned to 'policy'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:policy:spec-first", "kind": "policy"}. Omit if no canonical policy entry applies.

command_ref.description: Canonical reference to the CLI command that enforces this governance file as a whole. Kind is structurally pinned to 'command'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:command:governance-check", "kind": "command"}. Omit when no single command does. A rule of 'rules' names its own command in 'cli_command'.
